title: Strings: Manipulating Text 🧵
description: Slice, dice, and combine text – essential for crafting exploits and parsing output.

slides.title: Strings are Everywhere
slides.content:
# In Hacking, Everything is Text

Banners, HTTP responses, file paths, usernames, passwords – all strings. Python gives you incredible powers to slice, search, and transform text.

```python
banner = "SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_8.9p1 Ubuntu-3ubuntu0.6"
```
We can extract the version, check for vulnerabilities, and more.

slides.title: String Basics
slides.content:
# Quotes and Multi‑line

* Single or double quotes: `'hello'` `"hello"`
* Triple quotes for multiple lines:
```python
payload = """GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
"""
```
* Empty string: `""` or `''`

quizData.question: What is `len("hack")`?
quizData.explanation: The string has four characters: h, a, c, k.

slides.title: Indexing – Zero‑Based Positions 🔢
slides.content:
# Characters Have Addresses

Each character has an index starting from 0:
```
String:  P  y  t  h  o  n
Index:   0  1  2  3  4  5
```
You can access with `string[index]`:
```python
lang = "Python"
print(lang[0])  # P
print(lang[5])  # n
```

slides.title: Negative Indexing 🔙
slides.content:
# Count from the End

Use negative numbers to start from the right:
```python
s = "Python"
s[-1]  # n
s[-2]  # o
```
Great for grabbing file extensions: `filename[-3:]` for `.py`

slides.title: Slicing – Getting Substrings ✂️
slides.content:
# The Power of [start:stop:step]

* `s[start:stop]` – from `start` up to but NOT including `stop`
* `s[:stop]` – from beginning to stop
* `s[start:]` – from start to end
* `s[:]` – whole copy
* `s[::-1]` – reverse!

```python
ip = "192.168.1.100"
first_octet = ip[0:3]   # "192"
last_part = ip[-3:]     # "100"
```

slides.title: Slicing Practice
slides.content: Extract the domain from an email:
slides.codeSnippet:
email = "admin@example.com"
at_index = email.find('@')
domain = email[at_index+1:]
print(domain)  # example.com

slides.title: String Concatenation & Repetition
slides.content:
# Combine and Repeat Strings

* Concatenate with `+` : `"Hello" + " " + "World"`
* Repeat with `*` : `"-=" * 20` → `"-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-="`

```python
target = "192.168.1." + "1"
separator = "=" * 40
```

slides.title: Building a Banner
slides.codeSnippet:
tool = "CybronScanner"
line = "=" * len(tool)
print(line)
print(tool)
print(line)

slides.title: String Methods – Built‑in Power
slides.content:
# Python Strings Come with Tools

* `upper()`, `lower()` – change case
* `strip()` – remove whitespace
* `replace(old, new)` – swap text
* `split(sep)` – divide into list
* `startswith(prefix)`, `endswith(suffix)`
* `find(sub)` – locate substring

```python
payload = "  admin:admin  "
clean = payload.strip()   # "admin:admin"
```

slides.codeSnippet:
banner = "SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_8.9p1"
if banner.startswith("SSH"):
    version = banner.split("_")[-1]

quizData.question: What does `"  data  ".strip()` return?
quizData.explanation: strip() removes leading and trailing whitespace.

slides.title: Strings are Immutable
slides.content:
# You Can't Change a String In‑Place

```python
s = "hack"
s[0] = "H"  # TypeError!
```
Instead, create a new string:
```python
s = "H" + s[1:]  # "Hack"
```
Keep this in mind when modifying payloads.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use `in` for Substring Checking

```python
if "vulnerable" in banner:
    print("Possible exploit!")
```
`in` returns a boolean – super handy.
